title: Tissue Engineering
description: Tissue Engineering introduces students to the engineering of living constructs for repair, regeneration, disease modeling, and translational biomedical applications. The course integrates cell sources, extracellular matrix, scaffold materials, cell-material interactions, biochemical signals, bioreactors, transport limits, tissue characterization, tissue-specific applications, and regulatory translation.

topics.title: Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine Foundations
topics.description: Students begin with the field's core design logic: combine cells, materials, biochemical signals, and physical cues to repair, replace, or regenerate tissue function.

children.title: Field overview
children.description: The point is to understand tissue engineering as an integration of biology, materials science, and engineering design.

children.title: In vitro models and therapeutic constructs
Design constraints
children.description: Students learn why engineered tissues must satisfy biological, mechanical, transport, and manufacturing constraints at once.

children.title: Historical and translational context
children.description: This subtopic frames how the field developed and why translation remains challenging.

topics.title: Cell Sources and Stem-Cell Biology
topics.description: This module examines where therapeutic or experimental cells come from and how their phenotype, potency, and culture conditions shape tissue-engineered constructs.

children.title: Cell source selection
children.description: Students learn to choose cells based on availability, function, expansion capacity, and immune compatibility.

children.title: Stem-cell potency and differentiation
children.description: Stem cells are useful because they can self-renew and produce specialized cells under the right cues.

children.title: Cell culture fundamentals
children.description: Reliable tissue engineering depends on controlled, sterile, reproducible cell culture.

topics.title: Extracellular Matrix Structure and Function
topics.description: Students learn how native ECM provides biochemical, mechanical, and architectural cues that guide tissue development and repair.

children.title: ECM composition
children.description: The ECM is not just filler; it is a dynamic biochemical and mechanical environment.

children.title: ECM signaling
children.description: Students learn how cells read matrix cues and convert them into behavior.

children.title: ECM remodeling
children.description: Tissues mature and heal through synthesis, degradation, and reorganization of matrix.

topics.title: Scaffold Materials and Fabrication
topics.description: This topic focuses on designing material environments that support cell attachment, organization, growth, degradation, and tissue formation.

children.title: Material classes
children.description: Scaffolds are chosen for mechanics, degradation, chemistry, manufacturability, and biocompatibility.

children.title: Fabrication methods
children.description: Students learn how scaffold architecture is created and controlled.

children.title: Scaffold design properties
children.description: The design must support cells while evolving as tissue forms.

topics.title: Cell-Material Interactions and Host Response
topics.description: Students study how cells, proteins, immune cells, and tissues respond when engineered materials are introduced.

children.title: Protein adsorption and adhesion
children.description: The first biological layer on a material often determines how cells respond.

children.title: Cell behavior on materials
children.description: Students learn how surfaces and mechanics guide cell fate and tissue formation.

children.title: Host response
children.description: Implanted constructs must manage inflammation, fibrosis, infection, and integration.

topics.title: Growth Factors, Morphogens, and Biochemical Signaling
topics.description: This module covers how soluble and immobilized signals regulate proliferation, migration, differentiation, and spatial organization.

children.title: Signal types
children.description: Biochemical signals instruct cells to divide, migrate, differentiate, or organize.

children.title: Delivery strategies
children.description: Students learn how signal presentation affects timing, location, and dose.

children.title: Signal design challenges
children.description: Effective signaling must balance potency, stability, cost, and safety.

topics.title: Bioreactors and Mechanical Stimulation
topics.description: Students learn how controlled culture systems provide transport, perfusion, strain, compression, shear, or electrical cues for tissue maturation.

children.title: Bioreactor roles
children.description: Bioreactors provide controlled environments that static culture cannot.

children.title: Mechanical cues
children.description: Many tissues require physical stimulation to mature properly.

children.title: Scale-up and control
children.description: Students connect bench culture to repeatable production.

topics.title: Vascularization and Mass-Transport Limits
topics.description: This topic addresses one of tissue engineering's central bottlenecks: keeping cells alive and functional in thick or metabolically active constructs.

children.title: Transport limits
children.description: Cells need oxygen and nutrients, and diffusion alone often fails in thick constructs.

children.title: Vascularization strategies
children.description: Students learn approaches for forming or supporting blood-supply networks.

children.title: Modeling and design
children.description: Transport calculations help estimate whether a construct can survive and mature.

topics.title: Tissue Characterization, Imaging, and Functional Testing
topics.description: Students learn how engineered tissues are evaluated using structural, biochemical, mechanical, and biological assays.

children.title: Structural characterization
children.description: Students learn how to observe scaffold and tissue organization.

children.title: Biochemical and cellular assays
children.description: Assays determine whether cells are alive, differentiated, and producing matrix.

children.title: Mechanical and functional testing
children.description: Engineered tissues must be judged by performance, not appearance alone.

topics.title: Tissue-Specific Engineering Applications
topics.description: This module compares strategies for bone, cartilage, skin, vascular, cardiac, neural, and organoid systems.

children.title: Musculoskeletal tissues
children.description: Bone and cartilage examples show how mechanics, mineralization, and matrix organization drive design.

children.title: Soft and vascular tissues
children.description: Students compare designs where elasticity, perfusion, and barrier function are central.

children.title: Advanced biological models
children.description: Organoids and organ-on-chip systems show how tissue engineering supports research and drug testing.

topics.title: Translation, Immunogenicity, Regulation, and Ethics
topics.description: Students connect laboratory design to clinical translation, immune compatibility, manufacturing, quality systems, regulatory pathways, and ethical concerns.

children.title: Immunogenicity and safety
children.description: Clinical constructs must avoid harmful immune, infection, tumor, or degradation responses.

children.title: Manufacturing and regulation
children.description: Students learn why reproducible manufacturing and quality systems are central to translation.

children.title: Ethical and societal issues
children.description: Tissue engineering raises questions about cell sourcing, consent, access, and responsible innovation.

children.title: Equity, cost, and clinical trial responsibility

topics.title: Design of a Tissue-Engineered Construct
topics.description: The course closes with an integrated design project where students justify cells, scaffolds, signals, culture conditions, testing plans, and translational constraints.

children.title: Design requirements
children.description: Students define what the construct must do before choosing technology.

children.title: Integrated construct design
children.description: The project requires choices that fit together biologically and practically.

children.title: Signals, bioreactor conditions, and culture timeline
Validation and translation plan
children.description: Students propose how to test whether the design works and what would be needed for translation.
